title: The 10 Best Air Hose Reels
subtitle: Retractable and manual air hose reels for garage and shop compressors, ranked from live Amazon data.
intro: An air hose reel keeps your compressor hose off the floor and out from under your feet. We ranked 10 best-sellers from VEVOR, AIRZILLA, Giraffe Tools, Flexzilla, Goodyear, DEWALT, Lincoln and others on rating, review volume and features (a hose included, auto rewind, a steel reel and a guide arm or swivel bracket). Most people want a 50 ft retractable reel with the hose included.

changelog.note: Page published with 10 ranked picks and 1 tool to avoid.

products.name: VEVOR Retractable Air Hose Reel, 3/8 in x 50 ft Hybrid Hose, 300 PSI

avoid.name: Amazon Basics Retractable Air Hose Reel - Fits 3/8-Inch 50-Feet Air Compressor Hoses, Hoses Excluded
avoid.flag: Retractable reel with no hose; VEVOR's with hose costs about the same
avoid.verdict: A spring-retract reel sold without a hose, for about the price of reels that include one.
reasons: The title says 'Hoses Excluded'. You have to buy a 50 ft hose separately and wind it onto a tensioned spring reel yourself.
The VEVOR retractable reel with a 50 ft hybrid hose (B0C36SR3TM) costs about $3 more, so the bare reel saves almost nothing.
It's rated 4.3 stars, below every retractable reel we rank except DEWALT's.

buyers_guide.a: Spring-retractable reels pull the hose back with a tug; they're the most convenient for a garage. Manual crank reels are cheaper, hold longer hoses, and suit people who already own hose.

buyers_guide.q: What hose length do I need?
buyers_guide.a: Measure from the reel to the farthest point you'll work, then add 10 feet. 50 ft covers a two-car garage from a wall mount; 65 ft and up suits bigger shops or driveways.
Hybrid polymer hose is light and kink-resistant. Rubber hose is heavier but lays flat and stays supple in the cold. Flexzilla's hose is famously flexible.
On a wall or ceiling stud near the compressor, with a short lead-in hose from the compressor to the reel. Use the swivel bracket so the hose pays out in any direction.
Yes for nailers, impact wrenches and inflating tires. 1/2-inch hose is only worth it for long runs to high-demand tools.
